mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior 5-quarter average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions depressing near-term corporate investment plans.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-quarter moving average
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rates in late-cycle tightening phases
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-increase baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the 5-quarter moving average proxy fails to predict direction with Rank IC > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces wage growth expectations and dampens equity discount rates.
regime_hint: Elevated unemployment and slowing wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under the trigger are not statistically superior to a control window (p > 0.10) or the IC < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (industrial production) exceeds its prior quarter average by at least 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive due to stronger near-term economic momentum and reduced risk aversion.
regime_hint: Recovery phase with rising production momentum
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under the trigger are negative or flat, and the IC < 0.05 over the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% for two months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening supply-side capacity and rising recession risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prior month for two consecutive months with drop ≥ 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under the trigger are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) or the IC > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month for the second consecutive month during a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 60-day forward return turns negative as inflation expectations rise and equity discount rates widen.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month increase > 0.5% for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under the trigger are not statistically worse than a baseline (p > 0.10) or the interaction IC < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 10,000 in a single month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market absorption outpaces supply and boosts investor confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under the trigger are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) or the IC < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months during a normalization phase, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative as demand softens and corporate earnings expectations decline.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < prior month by > 5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Demand normalization with softening retail activity
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under the trigger are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) or the IC > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP chained) of at least 2% for three months in a row predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening aggregate demand and elevated recession risk.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prior month for three consecutive months with drop ≥ 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under the trigger are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) or the IC < 0.05 over the 60-day window.
